Who among the following was the leader of the Moderates?
x: Gokhale The early Indian National Congress was divided into Moderates and Extremists. Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the leading figure of the Moderate faction. He believed in constitutional methods and gradual reform.

s: Who accused Indian National Congress of practising ‘politics of prayer, petition and protest’?
x: The first two decades are INC are described in history as a moderate era. Among some of the prominent moderate leaders were Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendra Nath Banerjee, Mahadev Govind Ranade, Pherozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Anand Mohan Bose. They had a sense of confidence in British justice and their generosity. Their aim was not aggressive nationalism for attaining independence. Leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, raised extremist ideology. B.G. Tilak accused moderates of believing in constitutional method and favouring the policy of protest, prayer, and petition.

s: Who among the following leaders was a supporter of ‘Swadeshi’?
x: Aurobindo Ghose was the main leader of Swadeshi Movement (started in 1905 A.D.) which began against the Bengal partition. Other main leaders of this movement were Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra) and Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal).

s: The protest method of moderate leaders of the Congress was ?
x: The methods employed by the two groups (Moderates and Extremists) of Congress were different in their tempo and approach. Congress split into two different groups at Surat Session of Congress in 1907 A.D. While the moderates had infinite faith in the efficacy of constitutional agitation and in appealing to the British sense of justice and fair play, in holding an annual conference, making speeches, passing elaborate resolutions and sending deputations to England. The extremists had no faith in the benevolence of British public or Parliament, nor were they convinced of the efficacy of merely holding conferences. Extremists had faith in the concept of passive resistance.

s: Who among the following led the Swadeshi Movement in Delhi?
x: Syed Haidar Raja led the Swadeshi movement in Delhi; Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were not associated with Delhi in this role.

s: Who among the following was not known as a moderate in the National Movement?
x: Tilak was a militant Extremist leader, whereas Naoroji, Ranade and Gokhale were Moderates, so Tilak is the one not known as a moderate.

s: Which one of the following leaders belonged to the Extremist wing of the Congress?
x: Aurobindo Ghose was an extremist of Congress. He was one of the four pillars (Lal, Bal, Pal, Ghose) of extremists. He was arrested in 1908 A.D. by British Police in Maniktalla garden raid. He got the punishment of one-year imprisonment, but he was released due to the lack of evidence. Finally, he became sage, secluded himself from revolutionary activities and moved to Pondicherry (Puducherry).

s: The Congress policy of prayer and petition ultimately came to an end under the guidance of:
x: Congress policy of prayer and petition ultimately came to an end or reduced to minimum under the leadership of Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He was one of the strongest opponent of the British Empire. He strongly recommended a method of agitation. Many intellectual Congressmen became his followers. Leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai of Punjab and Bipin Chandra Pal of Calcutta turned into staunch followers of him. They strongly opposed the moderate policies of Congress.

s: The first leader to use the word ‘Swaraj’ was :
x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s (1856-1920 A.D.) popular statement was ‘Swaraj is my birthright, I shall have it”. Although the word ‘Swaraj’ was first used by ‘Dayanand Saraswati.’ Option (a) might be the closest answer.

s: Who among the following was an extremist?
x: After the year 1906 A.D., the effect of extremism had increased on the Indian National Movement. The Congress split at Surat came in December 1907 A.D., around the time when revolutionary terrorism had gained momentum. The extremists were aggressive nationalist members of Indian National Congress. The important extremist leaders were Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghose. Tilak announced that ‘’ Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’’.

s: With reference to Indian Freedom Struggles, who among the following was labelled as ‘Moderate’ leader in the Congress?
x: Gokhale was a Moderate, whereas Pal, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo were Extremists.

s: Who accused Indian National Congress of practising politics of, pray and petition and protest?

s: Out of the below, a prominent leader of militant nationalist thought was?
x: Tilak was a militant Extremist leader, while Ranade, Gokhale and G.V. Joshi were Moderates.

s: What was the main objective of the Extremists or Assertive Nationalists?
o: Swaraj or complete independence from English rule
x: The Extremists, or Assertive Nationalists, aimed at Swaraj, meaning complete independence from British rule. Constitutional agitation, negotiation and gradual self-government were Moderate ideas.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Moderates were associated with the period 1885–1905.
Moderates sought more immediate Swaraj than the Extremists.
Extremists showed increasing distrust of British rule.
Extremists favoured agitation and mass mobilisation.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Moderates wanted gradual reform through petitions, while the Extremists demanded more immediate Swaraj. The Moderate phase was 1885–1905, and the Extremists distrusted British rule and used agitation.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the methods of the Extremists is incorrect?
o: They accepted Prayer, Petition and Protest as their principal method.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Extremists rejected Prayer, Petition and Protest, which was the Moderate method. They favoured self-sacrifice, mass movement and aggressive resistance.

s: What was the aim of the Moderates?
x: The Moderates sought gradual self-government through constitutional agitation; the Extremists sought Swaraj.

s: Which pair consists only of representative Moderate leaders?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh
x: Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale were both Moderates. Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh were Extremists, so every other pair includes an Extremist.

s: Which one of the following was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremists?
x: Aurobindo Ghosh was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremist wing.

s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
x: The Maharashtra extremist group was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak; Bengal was associated with Pal and Aurobindo, and Punjab with Lala Lajpat Rai.

s: Which group wanted to extend the Swadeshi-Boycott movement more widely?
o: The British Committee of the INC
x: It was the Extremists who wanted to widen the Swadeshi-Boycott movement; the Moderates were reluctant.

s: How did the Extremists compare with the Moderates on social reform?
x: The Moderates were generally pro-reform while the Extremists were comparatively orthodox; Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill.

s: Which of the following was a criticism of Extremist politics?
o: Its religious symbolism alienated Muslims and its social outlook was orthodox.
It weakened the demand for Swaraj by supporting colonial rule.
It completely rejected all cultural symbols.
It prevented the use of boycott and Swadeshi.
x: The Extremists were criticised for using religious symbolism that alienated Muslims and for being socially orthodox. The Surat Split was also regarded as weakening the Congress.

s: The '3 Ss' method – self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will – belonged to which group?
x: The 3 Ss were the Extremists' method; the 3 Ps (prayers, petitions, protests) were the Moderates'.

s: Which bill did Tilak oppose, showing the Extremists' comparatively orthodox stand on social reform?
x: Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill; the Extremists were comparatively orthodox on social reform.

s: Which one of the following defines extremist ideology during the early phase of Indian freedom movement?
o: Stimulating the production of indigenous articles by giving them preference over imported commodities
Obtaining self-government by aggressive means in place of petitions and constitutional ways
Providing national education according to the requirements of the country
Organising coups against the British empire through military revolt
x: The Extremists in the early national movement opposed the Moderates' "mendicant policy" of petitions and appeals. Leaders such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai demanded Swaraj and favoured assertive, direct action over purely constitutional methods. They promoted boycott, Swadeshi and national education to mobilise the masses, marking a shift towards active and confrontational politics for selfgovernment.

x: Moderates believed in constitutional methods of British Laws, adopting proposals and delegations to London for negotiation and discussion. On the other hand, extremists believed in aggressive protests, self-sacrifices and determination at the beginning of the Indian Independence Movement. Independence meant for extremists as Complete Independence from foreign control, while moderates meant Independence as self-governance under colonial rule.

s: Who propounded the doctrine of ‘Passive Resistance’?
x: The principle of ‘’Passive Resistance’’ was propounded by Aurobindo Ghosh in his newspaper ‘’Vande Mataram’’. He was of the view that Britishers must immediately leave India. Indians must continue to protest until they leave India.

extremists’ policy of harping on Hindu past.

s: What did 'Atmashakti' mean in Extremist ideology?
x: Atmashakti meant self-reliance. It was connected with constructive work such as the establishment of cooperatives.

s: What was the main contribution of the Extremists to the national movement?
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a method associated with extremist nationalism?
x: The Extremists had no faith in British generosity. Their methods included passive resistance, mass agitation, boycott, Swadeshi, national education and self-sacrifice.

s: How did spiritual nationalism view the nation?
x: Spiritual nationalism represented the nation as a mother goddess, an idea expressed through symbols such as Bande Mataram and Bhavani Mandir.

s: Aurobindo set out the doctrine of passive resistance in which paper?
x: Aurobindo set out passive resistance in Bande Mataram; Indu Prakash carried his earlier New Lamps for Old.

When did Bal Gangadhar Tilak get the title Lokmanya?
x: In June 1897 A.D., the Chapekar brothers attacked Rand, the president of the Plague Committee of Poona and killed Lieutenant Ayerst. It was alleged that the Brahmins of Poona, under the leadership of Tilak, had conspired in the murder of Rand and Ayerst. In July 1897 A.D., Tilak was arrested on charges of sedition under section 124-A of the Indian Penal Code for inciting murder through his writings. He was prosecuted and sentenced to 18 months imprisonment, which caused huge protests across the country. For this reason Tilak became popular as an all India leader and the public gave him the title of 'Lokmanya'.

he started the Shivaji and Ganpati festivals

s: K.M. Panikkar referred to whom as 'the first diplomat of modern India'?
x: K.M. Panikkar referred to Gopal Krishna Gokhale as 'the first diplomat of modern India.' Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent political leader, social reformer, and an important figure in India's struggle for independence. Panikkar praised Gokhale's political perspective, especially his peaceful methods and efforts to gain international support for India's cause, which laid the foundation for modern India's diplomatic strategies.

s: Who of the following is known as ‘Deshbandhu’?
x: Chittaranjan Das, a revolutionary freedom fighter, was endearingly called ‘Deshabandhu’ (Friend of the Country). Das was a lawyer by profession and made a name for himself when he returned to India after finishing his studies abroad, took up a law practice and defended Sri Aurobindo Ghosh in a court suit filed against him. After the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement, he became disillusioned and proposed a strategy to end dyarchy, but Congress did not accept it. He formed his own party Swaraj Party along with Motilal Nehru.

s: Four resolutions were passed at the famous Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906. The question of either retention OR rejection of these four resolutions became the cause of a split in Congress at the next Congress session held at Surat in 1907. Which one of the following was not one of those resolutions?
x: The 1906 Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress (INC) was a pivotal event in the Indian freedom struggle, marking the official shift from purely constitutional petitions to a more assertive nationalist agenda. Key Highlights:  President: The session was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the "Grand Old Man of India". He was chosen as a compromise candidate to bridge the growing rift between the Moderate and Extremist factions of the Congress.  Adoption of 'Swaraj': For the first time, the word Swaraj (Self-government) was used from the Congress platform as the ultimate goal of the Indian people. Naoroji declared that Swaraj, along the lines of selfgoverning British colonies (such as Canada and Australia), was the "only and chief remedy" for India's problems. • The Four Resolutions: The session is most famous for passing four historic resolutions that defined the Swadeshi movement:  Swaraj: Demand for self-rule.  Swadeshi: Promotion of indigenous goods and industries.  Boycott: Refusal to use British goods as a political tool.  National Education: Establishment of an educational system under national control, free from colonial influence.

s: Which one of the following movements has contributed to a split in the Indian National Congress resulting in the emergence of 'moderates' and 'extremists'?
x: The Swadeshi Movement, launched to oppose the Partition of Bengal, played a key role in splitting the Indian National Congress into Moderates and Extremists. The Extremists, led by figures such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Aurobindo Ghosh, sought to expand the Swadeshi and boycott movements beyond Bengal and extend the boycott to all forms of association with the colonial government. On the other hand, Moderates, led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Dadabhai Naoroji, preferred to confine the movements to Bengal and limit the boycott to foreign goods. The ideological differences culminated in a leadership tussle, and tensions escalated, leading to the formal split at the Surat Session of 1907.

x: Congress The Surat Split of 1907 was primarily the result of deep ideological differences between the Moderates and the Extremists within the Indian National Congress. The Extremists had lost faith in the Moderates' policy of constitutional agitation, petitions, and negotiations with the British Government, believing that these methods had failed to secure meaningful political concessions. Instead, they advocated more assertive methods such as the Swadeshi movement, boycott, national education, and passive resistance. Although the immediate trigger was a dispute over the election of the Congress President and the agenda of the Surat session, the underlying reason for the split was the Extremists' lack of confidence in the Moderates' approach.

s: Who was known as 'Andhra Tilak'?

x: The Extremist phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1917) began with the Swadeshi movement following the partition of Bengal. The Surat Split (1907) divided moderates and extremists. However, the Lucknow Pact (1916) occurred during the later phase when moderates regained influence.

x: Regulating Act - 1773 AD Partition of Bengal - 1905 AD Establishment of Muslim League - 1906 AD Surat split - 1907 AD

s: Indian National Movement came to be dominated by the extremists after –
x: After the year 1906 A.D., the effect of extremism had increased on the Indian National Movement. The Congress split at Surat came in December 1907 A.D., around the time when revolutionary terrorism had gained momentum. The extremists were aggressive nationalist members of Indian National Congress. The important extremist leaders were Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh. Tilak announced that ‘’ Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’’.

s: Some regions where extremist nationalism erupted during the period 1907–1919 are given below. Find the odd one among them.
x: The regional centres of Extremism were Maharashtra (Tilak), Bengal (Pal, Aurobindo) and Punjab (Lajpat Rai). Gujarat is not among them, so it is the odd one out.

s: Where did the Moderates and Extremists reunite after the Surat Split?
x: The reunion came at Lucknow in 1916, not in 1908; the split was followed by repression, the Newspapers Act of 1908 and Tilak's imprisonment.

s: Who led the Home Rule Movement?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
Lala Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo Ghosh
x: The Home Rule Movement was led by Tilak and Annie Besant; Das and Motilal Nehru led the Swaraj Party.

s: Which of the following sets of resolutions was associated with the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906?
o: Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, provincial autonomy, adult franchise and federation
Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India and Khilafat
Council entry, constitutional reform, Home Rule and communal award
x: The Calcutta session of 1906 passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education as a compromise between Moderates and Extremists.

s:

A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.

s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the order of these events?
o: The INC was founded before the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed after the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed before the founding of the INC
The Surat Split came after the formation of the Muslim League
x: INC 1885, partition 1905, Muslim League 1906, Surat Split 1907, so the League came after the INC, not before.

s: By 1917, how many Home Rule branches did Andhra have?
x: Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917.

s: After Annie Besant's arrest in June 1917, students of which Andhra college wore 'Besant lockets'?
x: Students of the Machilipatnam National College wore Besant lockets after her arrest on 15 June 1917.

s: Where was the first session of the INC (1885) held?
o: Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay
x: The first INC session met at Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, on 28-30 December 1885.

s: Which of the following was founded in 1875?
x: The Arya Samaj dates to 1875; Deoband dates to 1866 and the Ramakrishna Mission to 1897.

s: The Bijoliya Movement was started by Sadhu Sitaram Das. Who led it later?
x: Bijoliya was led by Sadhu Sitaram Das and later Vijay Singh Pathik; Nanautavi and Gangohi led Deoband.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Quit India began in 1942. Non-Cooperation began in 1920, Civil Disobedience in 1930 and the Arya Samaj was founded in 1875.

s: With which event did the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930 begin?
x: The Civil Disobedience Movement began with Gandhi's Dandi March and was led by Gandhi and the INC.

s: Who among the following was associated with the Quit India Movement?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942 and is a Quit India figure. Ashfaqulla Khan and Surya Sen were revolutionaries, and Sarojini Naidu is linked with Civil Disobedience.

s: Who presided over the Purna Swaraj session of the INC?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Purna Swaraj session.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Faraizi Movement was led by Haji Shariatullah. Champaran was led by Gandhi, Swadeshi by the nationalists and the Neo-Buddhist Movement by B.R. Ambedkar.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Bijoliya Movement was started by Sadhu Sitaram Das and later led by Vijay Singh Pathik.
The Deoband Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
The Neo-Buddhist / Dalit Buddhist Movement was led by B. R. Ambedkar.
The Faraizi Movement was started by Haji Shariatullah.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Deoband Movement (1866) was started by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, not Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, who led the Aligarh Movement. The Bijoliya, Neo-Buddhist and Faraizi pairings are right.

s: Which of the following statements is not correct?
o: The Arya Samaj Movement was associated with Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
The Ramakrishna Movement was associated with Swami Vivekananda.
The Aligarh Movement was associated with Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
The Neo-Buddhist / Dalit Buddhist Movement was associated with Swami Vivekananda.
x: Option D is incorrect: the Neo-Buddhist or Dalit Buddhist Movement was led by B. R. Ambedkar, not Swami Vivekananda, who is linked with the Ramakrishna Movement. The Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna and Aligarh pairings are right.

s: Which national educational institution was started at Machilipatnam in 1910?
x: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala (National College) at Machilipatnam was started in 1910 as part of the national education movement.

s: Which of the following did NOT take place during the Extremist phase of the national movement?
x: The Swadeshi Movement (1905), Surat Split (1907) and Tilak's Mandalay sentence (1908) fall in the Extremist phase; the Lucknow Pact (1916) came later.
